prs.body:
When creating an escrow, if the `CancelAfter` time is specified but the `FinishAfter` is not, the resulting escrow can be immediately completed using `EscrowFinish`. While this behavior is documented, it is unintuitive and can be confusing for users.

This commit introduces a new fix amendment (fix1571) which prevents the creation of new Escrow entries that can be finished immediately and without any requirements.

Once the amendment is activated, creating a new Escrow will require specifying the `FinishAfter` time explicitly or requires that a cryptocondition be specified.
prs.head: nbougalis:ripd1571

reviews.author: scottschurr
reviews.body: Nice work with the unit tests.  I found a few things you could consider changing, but none of them are mandatory.  Looks good.  :+1:

reviewCommentsList.author: scottschurr
reviewCommentsList.body: I'm under the impression that last sentence is no longer true for ILPv4.  But I could be wrong.

reviewCommentsList.author: scottschurr
reviewCommentsList.body: transactors -> transactions?

reviewCommentsList.author: scottschurr
reviewCommentsList.body: I gotta say, I really appreciate all the comments throughout this entire commit.  Thanks.  :+1:

reviewCommentsList.author: scottschurr
reviewCommentsList.body: I was going to gripe that `mark` should be a `NetClock::time_point`.  But I looked at the use model and it looks like you've done the right thing here.  I can't think of a way to make this interface more `chrono` without making the usage more complicated.

reviewCommentsList.author: scottschurr
reviewCommentsList.body:
FWIW, I had to study this `else` clause for several minutes before I determined the difference between it and the preceding `if`.  You could save that study time with a comment at the top of the `else` that said something like:
```
// Old rules: CancelAfter and FinishAfter must be after or equal to closeTime.
```
Not a requirement.  It just would have saved me some time.

reviewCommentsList.author: scottschurr
reviewCommentsList.body: I like the way you split this condition into two `if`s.  It's easier for me to think about.  However I think the first condition on this second `if` (`if [~sfCancelAfter]`) is redundant given the presence of the preceding `if`.  But I don't mind leaving the redundant condition since it makes the idiom consistent.  Your call.

reviewCommentsList.author: scottschurr
reviewCommentsList.body: You could hypothetically move the construction of `now` down a few lines to just before it's used.  But it's not that important.

reviewCommentsList.author: scottschurr
reviewCommentsList.body: I'm sure this was a pain, but I think the change from `condpay` and `lockup` to just `escrow` was a good idea.  It's way easier to read the unit tests in the context of the current terminology.  Thanks.

reviewCommentsList.author: scottschurr
reviewCommentsList.body:
Just as an alternative approach, I _think_ you can specify to `close()` exactly the amount of elapsed time you want between the previous `close()` and this one.  As this is coded there's a 5 second blurriness on the boundary.  By directly manipulating the elapsed `close()` time you may be able to test the precise boundaries you expect the `finish()` to `tec` or `tes`.  If that works I think it would be slightly better than the approach you're using.

If you choose to take that approach you might consider adding some `BEAST_ASSERTS` that `env.close()` advances to the places you expect.

This comment also applies to the `for` loops in the next three following "Timing:" tests.

reviewCommentsList.author: scottschurr
reviewCommentsList.body: It looks to me like this check and the one starting on line 447 are identical?  I'm okay running the same test with the amendment on and off.  But I'm not sure of the motivation for this particular repeated test vs any number of other tests.  No change required.  Just something to consider.

            env(finish("bob", "alice", seq),  condition(cb3),

```

reviewCommentsList.body: I struggled with this myself, and this was the best I could come up with in the absence of huge pain and big changes to allow an `STTimestamp` type field.

reviewCommentsList.author: nbougalis

reviewCommentsList.author: seelabs
reviewCommentsList.body:
If this were brand new code, I would agree with this semantics. However, requiring that finish after is one second more than cancel after is essentially the old semantic of `<=`.

What do you think about either:
1) Keeping the old `<=` semantic and reducing the number of changes in this PR.
or
2) Have a more meaningful time that cancel after must be greater than  finish after. One minute? Thirty seconds?

reviewCommentsList.author: seelabs
reviewCommentsList.body: This is tricky because it changes the semantics of existing escrows. Ideally, we'd like the new rules to apply to escrows created with the new rules. I don't know a good way to do this, and it's probably fine in this case.

reviewCommentsList.author: seelabs
reviewCommentsList.body: I agree with @scottschurr here. A one line comment saying with the difference between the two cases would be good.

reviewCommentsList.author: HowardHinnant
reviewCommentsList.body: Just got here, and ditto.  One _could_ turn `mark` into a `NetClock::time_point` just for the comparison, but it doesn't really buy you anything.

reviewCommentsList.body: The rationale is to ensure that the amendment doesn't "break" something that should be allowed.
